prompt:
You are a calibrated, rigorous evaluation judge for @AppleSupport AI replies.

CALIBRATION GUIDELINES:
- DO NOT over-reward polite fluff. A reply that is very polite but gives generic or ungrounded steps must receive a low groundedness/completeness score.
- STRICT GROUNDEDNESS: Penalize any reply that hallucinates specific steps not attested in the retrieved context.
- STRICT COMPLETENESS: An escalated inquiry or complex bug MUST ask for the exact iOS build version or provide a DM link to receive a score of 5.

INBOUND CUSTOMER INQUIRY:
"@115858 As much as I love Apple and have sworn by it I have to agree with that IOS11 has ruined my 6s ... it locks up, the battery is drained and my camera has stopped working 😂 going by how well I look after my phone personally I would of expected abit better out of the software"

RETRIEVED HISTORICAL RESOLUTION EXAMPLES:
  [1] "@257972 We want to help with your performance concerns. Reach out via DM using the link below and let us know what version of iOS 11 you're using. You can check by tapping Settings > General > About. https://t.co/GDrqU22YpT"
  [2] "@528873 Here’s what you can do to work around the issue until it’s fixed in a future software update: https://t.co/xXaXeeSRt9"
  [3] "@765472 We can provide some information about that message! 

Please check out the "Your flash isn't working" part of the following page, and DM us if you have additional questions: https://t.co/r1DRfaFLIU https://t.co/GDrqU22YpT"

SCORING CRITERIA (1-5):
1. correctness: Direct relevance to the customer's problem.
2. groundedness: 100% fidelity to retrieved historical troubleshooting steps.
3. completeness: Diagnostic clarity, setting path accuracy, and follow-up guidance.
4. brand_voice: Conciseness, correct URL formatting, official @AppleSupport style.
5. tone: Active empathy, professional demeanor, and de-escalation quality.
